passage.passage_text:
Jake, a sixth-grader, stood alone in the bustling schoolyard of his new school, located in the heart of the city. He had just moved to this unfamiliar place and was struggling to make new friends. The loneliness was overwhelming as he missed his old friends terribly.

Despite feeling lonely, Jake knew he had to be resilient. He decided he had to take a proactive approach to make friends in his new surroundings. He joined a local basketball team, attended neighborhood events, and even volunteered at a local library. Each of these steps were small but significant efforts in his quest to feel less alone.

Meanwhile, Lucy, a popular and friendly girl in Jake's class, noticed his efforts to integrate. She admired Jake's resilience and decided to lend him a helping hand. Her friendly nature and popularity among classmates made her the perfect person to bridge the gap between Jake and the rest of the class.

Seizing an opportunity, Lucy invited Jake to a party she was hosting. Jake was nervous but excited. At the party, Lucy made sure to introduce Jake to many of his classmates. Jake found himself having actual fun, laughing, and engaging in conversations with his peers. This event marked the beginning of many friendships for Jake.

Over time, Jake's friend circle grew. Thanks to Lucy's help and his own efforts, he now had an abundant number of friends. He was no longer the lonely new kid in the city. He felt a sense of belonging and was genuinely happy. He was grateful to Lucy for her help in his journey of making friends in the new city. The resilience he had shown in overcoming his loneliness turned his unfamiliar surroundings into a place he could call home.
